The terminal

The design of GA-124's research §5.1, §5.2 and §5.4 (docs/research/terminal.md): the sidebar's Terminal section, New terminal, the Terminal page, the Editor's terminal panel, one terminal in two places, the terminal's colours and the specs. TF0 builds the terminal's view and moves the tokens into the app, TF1 the sidebar and the page, TF2 the Editor's panel.

Every screen is drawn with the app's own stylesheets (src/styles), so it looks as the app will; the new components are in terminal.css and the new tokens in terminal-tokens.css (from new-tokens.json). The terminal's screen is a still picture of xterm.js in the term-* colours. Each screen shows dark, then light; the switch shows one theme. Hover a control for its tooltip. Built by node design/terminal/gen-terminal.mjs.

1. The sidebar's Terminal section

Between Projects and Editor, a section that folds like Editor, Agents and Memory: the same FoldSection, with "terminal" added to Fold and kept in gizai.sidebar.folded with the others. Its rows are the open terminals, oldest first, so a new one comes at the bottom and rows don't move under the pointer. There is no limit on how many.

  • Heading. “Terminal”, exactly as Editor's: + (New terminal) opens the folder picker (§2), the caret folds the section, and a click on the word folds it too. Folded, the heading says how many terminals are open, “3 open”, where Editor says “2 behind” and Agents “1 live”.
  • A row. Lucide terminal, the name, and on the right in text-3 what runs in it now: the program in mono (“npm”, “cargo”, “vim”), nothing while the shell waits for a command, or “ended” when the shell ended with a code other than 0. The folder, the shell and its state are in the row's tooltip. A click opens the terminal on its page (#/terminal/<id>); the row is selected while that page shows.
  • Names. The folder's name, then “gizai 2”, “gizai 3” for more in the same folder (the lowest free number). A card's worktree shows the card's identifier in mono and its title faint, as the Editor's card rows do. Rename (F2) sets any name up to 40 characters; an empty one gives the default back.
  • Never teal, never a pulse on a terminal's row: those mean an agent at work. What a terminal runs is your own work, so it is grey text.
  • No × on the row: a button inside a row that is a link isn't allowed (D2's rule), and the row stays quiet. Closing is in the row's menu, a middle click, and the × on the terminal's tab.
  • Right click (or the context menu key, or Shift+F10): Rename (F2), Show in Editor (opens the folder in the Editor with this terminal in its panel), Copy folder path, Close. The menu is the app's ContextMenu, as the Editor's rows have.
  • Close on a terminal that runs a program asks once, under the row, in one sentence: “npm is still running in gizai 2. Close it and end npm?”, with Close and Cancel; Enter closes, Escape cancels. A terminal that waits for a command, or has ended, closes at once.
  • None open: one row, “New terminal”, which opens the picker, as the Editor's “Open a folder” row does.
Dark

2. New terminal: the Editor's folder picker

+ on the Terminal heading (and New terminal when none is open) opens the Editor's folder picker, titled “New terminal in”, beside the sidebar: the same groups (Projects, the folders in ~/Herd, Cards), search box and footer. The folder the page shows is on top and chosen, so + then Enter starts another terminal there. Enter or a click starts a terminal in the chosen folder and opens its page; Escape closes the picker. Ctrl+Shift+` starts one at once in the folder you are in, without the picker.

  • Only the folders the Editor may open: projects' folders, the folders in ~/Herd and card worktrees, with the Editor's refusals; never your home folder. From there cd goes anywhere, as you: the rule decides where Gizai starts a shell, it doesn't fence the shell in.
  • A card an agent works on is in the list, off, with the pulse and who works (as in the Editor's picker); its tooltip says “QA Agent is working on GA-118: a terminal there waits until its run ends.”
  • A card that isn't pinned to you (another's, an agent's between runs, or nobody's): choosing it asks first, under its row, with the Editor's own button: “GA-112 is Frontend Agent's card: a shell there can change its files, as an edit can.” Edit anyway starts the terminal; Cancel keeps the picker open. A card pinned to you (by hand) starts at once.
  • From 20 open, a note on top of the list: “20 terminals are open: each keeps its shell running until you close it.” It never stops you: there is no limit.
Dark

3. The Terminal page

#/terminal/<id>. The top bar says which terminal and where it runs; under it the terminals of this terminal's folder as tabs (the same set as that folder's Editor panel, §4), then the terminal, which fills the rest. #/terminal without one is an empty page with New terminal.

  • Top bar. Terminal / gizai 2: a double-click (or F2) renames it in place. Then the folder in mono, the shell and its size in columns × rows, all in text-3; the size follows the place it shows in. Actions: Show in Editor (the folder in the Editor, with this terminal in its panel) and ⋯: Rename (F2), Find (Ctrl+Shift+F), Clear (empties the scrollback), Copy folder path, Close.
  • Tabs. The folder's terminals, drawn as the Editor's file tabs, size-term-tab high: the terminal icon, the name, the program that runs in it in mono, and ×. + starts another terminal in the same folder, without a picker. A double-click renames a tab in place; a middle click or × closes it, asking under the tab when a program runs. Ctrl+PgDn and Ctrl+PgUp step through them; ← and → move between tabs that have the focus.
  • The terminal fills the rest: term-bg (the code's background), 8px above and below and 12px at the sides, the mono font at the code size, the term-* colours (§6). The cursor is a block while the terminal has the focus and an outline while it hasn't, and it doesn't blink: only the live pulse moves on its own.
  • Find (Ctrl+Shift+F; Cmd+F on macOS): a small box at the top right, over the terminal, so the terminal keeps its size and full-screen programs don't redraw. The query in mono, Match case, Words and Regular expression inside the box, “3 of 12”, previous and next, close. Matches are marked as the Editor marks them: term-selection, the current one with an accent border.
  • Ended. exit with code 0 closes the terminal and its tab. Any other end keeps it, read-only, with a bar under the tabs: “The shell ended with exit code 2.” with Start again (a new shell in the same folder, the same name and tab) and Close; the screen stays as it was, to read, select and find in. The tab and the sidebar row say “ended”. A shell that never started says why: “Couldn't start zsh in ~/Herd/gizai: /usr/bin/zsh wasn't found.”, with Try again and Close.

4. The Editor with its terminal panel

The Editor's top bar gets a Terminal button between Fetch and Open in. It shows a panel in the code column, between the code and the status bar, with this folder's terminals as tabs; the file tree keeps its full height, as in VS Code's default layout. The status bar stays at the Editor's bottom edge, so it doesn't jump when the panel opens.

  • The button is a ghost button like Fetch (Lucide terminal, “Terminal”); without Fetch (no origin remote) it comes first. Pressed (aria-pressed, the selected fill) while the panel shows. Its tooltip says “Show the terminal (Ctrl+`)” or “Hide the terminal (Ctrl+`)”. When the folder has no terminal yet it starts one in the folder's root, which gets the focus.
  • Off, with the reason as its tooltip, while a terminal can't start there: an agent works on the card (“QA Agent is working on GA-118: a terminal there waits until its run ends.”), or the card isn't pinned to you and you haven't pressed Edit anyway (a shell can change files just as an edit can). Off is aria-disabled, not disabled, so the pointer and the keyboard still reach it and the tooltip shows.
  • A terminal opened before an agent started stays, with the Editor's bar over it. Then the button still shows and hides the panel (it starts nothing), and the panel's + is off with the same reason.
  • The panel is 30% of the column (.ed-main: the file tabs, the code, the panel and the status bar) the first time. Its top border is the drag handle: a 1px line with a 6px grab area, the row-resize pointer, 2px of accent on hover and while dragging. A double-click gives 30% back. Limits: at least 120px of code, and at least 120px of panel (its tabs and about 4 lines). The height is kept as a share, once for all folders (gizai.editor.panel), so it stays 30% when the window changes size; whether the panel shows is kept per folder, with its file tabs.
  • Its tabs: this folder's terminals, as on the Terminal page, with +; on the right Own page (the terminal on its page, #/terminal/<id>) and Hide (Ctrl+`). Hiding keeps every shell running; closing the last tab hides the panel.
  • Keys in the panel go to the shell: Ctrl+W, Ctrl+P and Ctrl+B don't reach the Editor while the terminal has the focus. Ctrl+` (hide), Ctrl+Shift+` (a new tab) and find still work.

5. One terminal, two places

A terminal is one shell with one screen, which moves to the place that shows it: the Terminal page or its folder's panel in the Editor. Open gizai 2 from the sidebar and its page has it; go back to the Editor and the panel has it again, with everything on it: its scrollback, what runs in it, its selection. It takes the size of the place, 120 × 12 in the panel and 132 × 38 on the page, and a full-screen program (vim, htop) redraws at the new size.

  • The place that asked last shows the terminal. Today one page shows at a time, so the place on screen always has it. When two places want it at once (a second window or a split, later), the other one shows a quiet line in the terminal's place, “gizai 2 is on its own page.”, with Show here, which moves it back.
  • The panel's tab says the same: its icon becomes Own page's (Lucide maximize-2) and its tooltip reads “gizai 2 is on its own page.”. On the page it reads “gizai 2 is in gizai's Editor.”.
  • Own page and Show in Editor are the two ways across; the sidebar's row stays the same row wherever the terminal shows.

6. The terminal's colours

Twenty-two new colour tokens, term-*, for dark and light, in design/terminal/new-tokens.json (design/tokens.json's format; TF0 moves them there). xterm.js takes colours as strings, so TF0 reads each token with getComputedStyle when a terminal starts and after each theme change (t, Settings → Appearance), and an alias such as {bg} arrives resolved.

  • One surface with the code. term-bg is bg, the code's background, and term-fg is text; the cursor is text as in the code, the selection the accent's blue, stronger than the code's, so a selection in output stands out.
  • Red and green are the Changes view's. term-red is diff-del and term-green diff-add, so git diff in a terminal reads as a card's Changes. Yellow is the gold of syn-type and blue the blue of syn-function.
  • Cyan and magenta keep away from Gizai's two signals. Teal live means an agent at work and magenta needs means “needs you”; a program's cyan and magenta are its own output. So term-cyan is a sky blue and term-magenta a violet: at least 35° of hue (OKLCH) and a ΔE2000 of at least 15 from both, in both themes. The generator refuses values that break this.
  • Contrast. Every colour a program prints as text is at least 4.5:1 on term-bg. Bright colours are the stronger ones on each background: lighter in dark, darker in light. Three are block colours, under 4.5:1 by nature (black in dark; white and bright white in light); xterm.js's minimumContrastRatio: 4.5 lifts any text that lands under 4.5:1, so a program's black text on the dark background still reads.
  • Never colour alone holds in the terminal too: programs print words with their colours (“ok”, “FAILED”, “modified:”), and Gizai adds no colour of its own to their output.

7. Specs: sizes, states, the font, keys

Sizes are tokens: the five new ones are in new-tokens.json (and terminal-tokens.css, which shows how they grow with the density and the Interface text size, as size-tab does); the rest are the app's spacing, text and radius tokens. States follow the design system: hover the hover fill, selected the selected fill, focus a 2px focus ring, off at 45%.

The font

  • The app's mono font at the code size: --font-mono, 12.5px on 20px lines (t-code), growing with the Interface text size as the code does (calc(12.5px + var(--ui-grow))). It follows Settings → Appearance (Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono, JetBrains Mono, Geist Mono or Hack); TF0 waits for the font to load before xterm.js measures its cells, and fits again when it changes.
  • xterm.js's options: fontFamily the computed --font-mono, fontSize 12.5 (+ the Interface step), lineHeight 1.6, fontWeight 400, fontWeightBold 700, drawBoldTextInBrightColors on, minimumContrastRatio 4.5, cursorStyle block, cursorInactiveStyle outline, cursorBlink off, scrollback 5000, customGlyphs and rescaleOverlappingGlyphs on.
  • Box drawing (tree, htop, git log --graph): the bundled fonts are cut to Latin and have none. With WebGL xterm.js draws them itself (customGlyphs). For the DOM renderer, TF0 adds a box-drawing subset (U+2500–259F) of JetBrains Mono, which the app ships already under the OFL, as a fallback after --font-mono for the terminal only, and checks that tree lines up.
  • No italic or bold of Gizai's own: a program that asks for bold gets the bright colour and the bold weight; one that asks for italic gets the browser's slant, since the fonts have no italic.

For screen readers and the keyboard

  • The sidebar's rows are links (“gizai 2, running npm”); the tabs a tablist, each × a button named “Close gizai 2”. The question under a row or tab is an alertdialog that takes the focus, Close first.
  • The terminal is xterm.js's own: TF0 turns on screenReaderMode when the system asks for it, so its rows are read as text.
  • The handle is a separator with the share in aria-valuenow and its name “Terminal panel's height”; the Terminal button says pressed or not; off, it stays focusable and its reason is its description.
  • Ended, couldn't start and the 20-open note are status (couldn't start is an alert), so they are read out when they appear.

8. Every text

Every heading, row, button, tooltip and sentence on these screens, in sentence case, in the order of the page. Names, paths and numbers are the examples'; TF0, TF1 and TF2 put in the real ones. The words on a sidebar row (“npm”, “ended”) stay lowercase, like Agents' “paused” and the Editor's “4 changed”. Group heads in the picker are set in capitals by CSS, as the Editor's are.
